practiceQuestions.q: Who was the Mughal Emperor immediately preceding Alamgir II?
practiceQuestions.sol: Ahmad Shah Bahadur reigned from 1748 to 1754 before he was blinded and deposed by Wazir Imad-ul-Mulk, who then installed Aziz-ud-din on the throne under the title Alamgir II. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 11 History]

practiceQuestions.q: What was the original personal name of Alamgir II before ascending the Mughal throne?
practiceQuestions.sol: Aziz-ud-din, a grandson of Emperor Jahandar Shah, was chosen by Wazir Imad-ul-Mulk and took the regnal title 'Alamgir II' upon his coronation in 1754. [Primary Reference: Standard Medieval History Canons]

practiceQuestions.q: During whose reign as Wazir was Alamgir II placed on the Mughal throne?
practiceQuestions.sol: Imad-ul-Mulk (Ghazi-ud-din Khan Feroz Jung III) served as the powerful and dictatorial wazir who deposed Ahmad Shah and placed Alamgir II as a puppet emperor in 1754. [Primary Reference: NCERT Themes in Indian History]

practiceQuestions.q: In which year did Alamgir II pass away / get assassinated?
practiceQuestions.sol: Alamgir II was assassinated in November 1759 by his wazir Imad-ul-Mulk, who feared the emperor's growing closeness to certain nobles and foreign elements. [Primary Reference: Bipan Chandra, Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q: Who was the notable son of Alamgir II who later became the Mughal Emperor under the title Shah Alam II?
practiceQuestions.sol: Prince Ali Gauhar was the eldest son of Alamgir II. He fled Delhi during the political turmoil and later assumed the imperial title Shah Alam II in exile. [Primary Reference: Spectrum Modern India]

practiceQuestions.q: Which foreign invader attacked and captured Delhi during the reign of Alamgir II in 1757?
practiceQuestions.sol: Ahmad Shah Abdali (Durrani) invaded India multiple times; during Alamgir II's reign, he entered Delhi in January 1757, plundered the city, and exacted heavy tributes. [Primary Reference: NCERT History]

practiceQuestions.q: What was the administrative status of Alamgir II within the Mughal governance structure?
opts: An absolute monarch with supreme executive power
A puppet ruler subservient to Wazir Imad-ul-Mulk
A powerful military general leading expansionist campaigns
A reformer who successfully revived the Mansabdari system
practiceQuestions.sol: Alamgir II was entirely a puppet ruler. Actual administrative and military powers were usurped by Wazir Imad-ul-Mulk, leaving the emperor virtually powerless in the Red Fort. [Primary Reference: NCERT Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q: The famous battle of Plassey took place in 1757, which falls precisely during the reign of which Mughal Emperor?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Battle of Plassey (June 1757) occurred when Alamgir II was the titular Mughal Emperor in Delhi, demonstrating the disconnect between events in Bengal and the central Mughal authority. [Primary Reference: Spectrum Modern India]

practiceQuestions.q: Which noble helped Ahmad Shah Abdali during his 1757 invasion and was appointed Mir Bakhshi?
practiceQuestions.sol: Rohilla chief Najib-ud-Daula aligned with Ahmad Shah Abdali during the 1757 invasion and was made Mir Bakhshi of the Mughal Empire to safeguard Afghan interests in Delhi. [Primary Reference: NCERT History]

practiceQuestions.q: What title was assumed by Aziz-ud-din upon becoming emperor, in emulation of which great Mughal emperor?
practiceQuestions.sol: Aziz-ud-din took the title 'Alamgir II', styling himself after the strict and powerful Emperor Aurangzeb (who used the title Alamgir, meaning 'Conqueror of the World'), though he lacked any of Aurangzeb's power. [Primary Reference: Medieval Indian History Textbooks]

practiceQuestions.q: How did the rise of Wazir Imad-ul-Mulk reflect the systemic decay of the Mughal central authority during Alamgir II's reign?
opts: It showed the successful centralization of power by competent bureaucratic elites.
It demonstrated that imperial succession and executive control had become playthings of opportunistic nobles and foreign kingmakers.
It established a permanent constitutional monarchy curbing imperial excesses.
It marked the harmonious cooperation between the Emperor and regional subedars.
practiceQuestions.sol: Imad-ul-Mulk's actions highlight the absolute hollow nature of the Mughal throne, where prime ministers acted as dictators, blinding and murdering emperors at will without facing any loyalist resistance. [Primary Reference: NCERT Themes in Indian History]

practiceQuestions.q: What was the primary geo-political consequence of Ahmad Shah Abdali's invasions during the tenure of Alamgir II?
opts: Complete integration of Punjab and Afghanistan into the Mughal Empire
Severe financial bankruptcy of the imperial treasury, depopulation of Delhi, and permanent loss of Punjab to Afghans
The signing of a treaty making Delhi a British protectorate
An alliance between the Mughals and Marathas that completely eradicated foreign threats
practiceQuestions.sol: Abdali's relentless incursions drained Delhi, exposed northern India's vulnerability, resulted in the loss of Punjab, and accelerated the collapse of the Mughal empire. [Primary Reference: Bipan Chandra, India's Struggle for Independence & History]

practiceQuestions.q: Analyze the role of the Marathas in Delhi politics during the reign of Alamgir II. How did they intervene?
opts: Marathas remained completely neutral and avoided northern affairs.
Maratha generals like Raghunath Rao entered Delhi, allied with Wazir Imad-ul-Mulk, and sought to dominate imperial administration to counter Afghan influence.
Marathas fought against Alamgir II to annex Delhi directly as a Maratha province.
Marathas acted as tax collectors exclusively for the East India Company.
practiceQuestions.sol: Invited or maneuvering through regional politics, Maratha forces under Raghunath Rao reached Delhi in 1758, expelling Najib-ud-Daula and establishing effective Maratha paramountcy over Delhi's puppet court. [Primary Reference: NCERT History]

practiceQuestions.q: Why did Wazir Imad-ul-Mulk ultimately assassinate Alamgir II in 1759?
opts: Alamgir II refused to convert to another religion.
Imad-ul-Mulk suspected the Emperor of conspiring with foreign invaders like Ahmad Shah Abdali and asserting independence against the Wazir's control.
Alamgir II failed to pay the British East India Company's annual tribute.
The Emperor launched a successful military coup that imprisoned Imad-ul-Mulk.
practiceQuestions.sol: Imad-ul-Mulk feared that Alamgir II was trying to escape his tutelage and inviting Ahmad Shah Abdali back to Delhi to eliminate the Wazir, prompting Imad-ul-Mulk to murder the Emperor. [Primary Reference: Advanced Study in the History of Modern India]

practiceQuestions.q: What does the phrase 'kingmaker' signify in the context of Delhi politics during the mid-18th century including Alamgir II's reign?
opts: The British Parliament passing acts to appoint governors general
Powerful nobles like Imad-ul-Mulk who manipulated the imperial succession, placing puppet emperors on the throne and deposing them at will
Sikh misls electing a supreme temporal leader in Punjab
The Mughal Emperor possessing divine authority to appoint regional kings
practiceQuestions.sol: While the Sayyid brothers were original kingmakers earlier in the 18th century, figures like Imad-ul-Mulk continued this tradition of absolute manipulation where the Mughal emperor became a dispensable puppet. [Primary Reference: NCERT Themes in Indian History]

practiceQuestions.q: How did the economic condition of the central Mughal domains change during the reign of Alamgir II?
opts: Unprecedented agricultural prosperity due to revenue reforms
Complete collapse of the Jagirdari crisis, unpaid imperial troops looting the city, and severe famine/poverty around Delhi
Accumulation of immense wealth from overseas trade ports
Establishment of a central bank by Alamgir II to issue paper currency
practiceQuestions.sol: The jagirs were severely depleted, revenues failed to reach the capital, soldiers mutinied for pay, and repeated plunder by Abdali left Delhi's economy in ruins. [Primary Reference: Satish Chandra, Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q: What was the significance of Prince Ali Gauhar's escape from Delhi during the reign of Alamgir II?
opts: It ended the Mughal dynasty permanently.
It ensured the survival of the imperial bloodline and enabled him to later assert claims in eastern India as Shah Alam II.
He successfully mobilized a pan-Indian army to defeat the British.
He surrendered all imperial titles to the East India Company.
practiceQuestions.sol: Fearing for his life from Wazir Imad-ul-Mulk, Ali Gauhar fled Delhi. He later became Shah Alam II and was involved in key events like the Battle of Buxar. [Primary Reference: Spectrum Modern India]

practiceQuestions.q: In what ways did the territorial extent of the Mughal Empire shrink during Alamgir II's reign?
opts: The empire expanded southward into the deep Deccan.
It was effectively restricted to a tiny pocket around Delhi and parts of the Doab, plagued by Rohillas, Marathas, and Jats.
Bengal and Awadh were annexed directly into the imperial crown lands.
The empire regained control over Kabul and Kandahar.
practiceQuestions.sol: The Mughal sway had shrunk so dramatically that the popular contemporary Persian couplet went: 'Sultanat-i-Shah Alam, az Dilli ta Palam' (The kingdom of the king is from Delhi to Palam). [Primary Reference: NCERT History]

practiceQuestions.q: How did regional powers like the Jats and Rohillas interact with the central Mughal administration under Alamgir II?
opts: They served as loyal provincial governors paying regular revenues.
They acted as autonomous power-brokers, frequently allying with or defying the Wazir and Emperor, and plundering imperial domains.
They completely integrated their military forces under direct imperial command.
They peacefully surrendered all their forts to Alamgir II.
practiceQuestions.sol: Jats under Suraj Mal and Rohillas under Najib-ud-Daula carved out independent spheres of influence, fighting among themselves and exploiting the weakness of Delhi's central government. [Primary Reference: Medieval Indian History]

practiceQuestions.q: What was the broader historical significance of the five-year reign of Alamgir II (1754–1759)?
opts: It marked the renaissance of Mughal art, architecture, and literature.
It represented the terminal phase of the Mughal Empire's disintegration, setting the stage for direct foreign hegemony (Maratha and British).
It initiated a century of successful agrarian reforms across northern India.
It solidified Mughal alliances with European trading companies.
practiceQuestions.sol: Alamgir II's reign encapsulates the tragic endgame of the Mughals: external invasions by Abdali, internal tyranny by Imad-ul-Mulk, Maratha dominance, and the final drift toward British colonial ascendancy. [Primary Reference: Bipan Chandra, History of Modern India]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Alamgir II:
1. He was the immediate successor of Muhammad Shah on the Mughal throne.
2. His reign witnessed the third invasion of Ahmad Shah Abdali and the capture of Delhi.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because Alamgir II was the successor of Ahmad Shah Bahadur, not Muhammad Shah (Ahmad Shah succeeded Muhammad Shah). Statement 2 is correct; Abdali invaded in 1757 during Alamgir II's reign, plundering Delhi and Mathura. [Primary Reference: NCERT History]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about Wazir Imad-ul-Mulk during the reign of Alamgir II:
1. He was a powerful and ambitious minister who exercised absolute control over the imperial administration.
2. Ultimately, he had Alamgir II assassinated in 1759 out of political suspicion.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Imad-ul-Mulk functioned as a dictator, reducing Alamgir II to a complete puppet, and later assassinated him in November 1759 when he suspected the Emperor was plotting against him with Abdali. [Primary Reference: Standard Medieval History Sources]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the geopolitical developments during Alamgir II's reign:
1. The Battle of Plassey was fought in Bengal during his tenure as the titular Mughal Emperor.
2. Maratha forces under Raghunath Rao entered Punjab and Delhi during this period.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. The Battle of Plassey occurred in June 1757 under Alamgir II's nominal reign. Simultaneously, Marathas expanded aggressively into northern India, capturing Delhi in 1758 under Raghunath Rao. [Primary Reference: Spectrum Modern India & NCERT History]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Najib-ud-Daula:
1. He was a Rohilla chief who allied with Ahmad Shah Abdali against the Mughal Wazir.
2. He was appointed as Mir Bakhshi of the Mughal Empire during Alamgir II's reign.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Najib-ud-Daula backed Abdali during the 1757 invasion and was rewarded with the high military office of Mir Bakhshi to protect Afghan interests at the Mughal court. [Primary Reference: NCERT History]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about Prince Ali Gauhar (later Shah Alam II):
1. He was the son of Alamgir II.
2. He successfully retained full control over Delhi and Punjab throughout his father's reign.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct; Ali Gauhar was Alamgir II's eldest son. Statement 2 is incorrect because Ali Gauhar had to flee Delhi due to threats from Wazir Imad-ul-Mulk and spent years in exile, never maintaining control over Punjab (which fell to Abdali/Sikhs). [Primary Reference: Spectrum Modern India]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the state of the Mughal Army during the reign of Alamgir II:
1. The central army was well-funded, disciplined, and capable of projecting imperial power across India.
2. Soldiers frequently rioted for arrears of pay, and the military apparatus was completely dependent on mercenary groups and regional warlords.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect as the imperial army was financially ruined, weak, and undisciplined. Statement 2 is correct; unpaid soldiers rioted in the streets of Delhi, and defense relied entirely on external actors like Marathas or Afghan mercenaries. [Primary Reference: Satish Chandra, Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the cultural and architectural developments under Alamgir II:
1. Large-scale imperial construction projects flourished in Delhi, rivaling the monuments of Shah Jahan.
2. Due to extreme financial bankruptcy and political insecurity, royal patronage for arts and monumental architecture dried up almost completely.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect as no major architectural monuments were built during this era. Statement 2 is correct; poverty, frequent foreign raids, and administrative chaos meant the court had neither funds nor peace to patronize monumental arts. [Primary Reference: An Introduction to Indian Art, NCERT]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the relationship between the Mughal Emperor Alamgir II and the Marathas:
1. Alamgir II viewed the Marathas strictly as enemies and refused any diplomatic engagement with them.
2. Maratha intervention in Delhi was necessitated by the need to check Afghan dominance under Ahmad Shah Abdali and secure financial tributes from northern territories.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because the puppet court under Wazir and Emperor had to accept Maratha protection at various points to survive against Abdali. Statement 2 is correct; Marathas intervened aggressively in Delhi to counter Afghan power and extract resources. [Primary Reference: NCERT Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements concerning the political fragmentation during the Later Mughal period:
1. Regional governors in Awadh, Bengal, and Hyderabad established effective de facto independence while maintaining nominal allegiance to Delhi.
2. The emperor Alamgir II possessed the military capacity to suppress these provincial dynasties and restore imperial centralization.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct; states like Awadh (Safdarjung), Bengal (Alivardi Khan/Siraj), and Hyderabad functioned independently while recognizing the Mughal emperor as the titular fountainhead of authority. Statement 2 is completely false; Alamgir II was utterly toothless and lacked any military capacity. [Primary Reference: Bipan Chandra, History of Modern India]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the assassination of Alamgir II:
1. He was killed by his wazir, Imad-ul-Mulk, in November 1759 under the pretext of visiting a holy man.
2. Following his murder, Imad-ul-Mulk immediately crowned himself as the new Mughal Emperor.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct; Alamgir II was lured to Kotla Firoz Shah on the pretext of meeting a pious ascetic and was murdered by Imad-ul-Mulk's henchmen. Statement 2 is incorrect because Imad-ul-Mulk did not crown himself; instead, he placed Shah Jahan III on the throne as another puppet emperor. [Primary Reference: Advanced Study in the History of Modern India]
